implementation_notes: No language offers an envy detector or a remedy API; this is a judgement plus a sequence of refactorings. The test is quantitative and language-neutral: in one method, count the distinct fields and operations of the enclosing type against those of another type — if the other type dominates, the method is envious. The Fowler/Beck procedure is: if only part of the method is envious, Extract Method/Function on that part; then Move Method/Move Function onto the type that holds most of the data the method uses. Where a function uses several types, split it first so each piece goes to the type holding its data. In a language with no user-definable types (a struct-of-arrays kernel), the destination is a function over the record rather than a method on it.
idiom_name: Move Method / Move Function, preceded by Extract Method or Extract Function
pitfalls: Counting references will flag mappers, DAOs and serializers, which are envious by construction; the count is a prompt, not a verdict.
Moving a method that needs the old class as a parameter means the envy was a symptom, not the cause.
Moving repeatedly until nothing is envious can produce a class of pure forwarders — a middle man.
